page.title: Reader
page.purpose: Show the original page beside the units derived from it, with selection linking the two in both directions, so a human can see exactly what the machine understood and correct it where it was wrong.

priorities.statement: Selecting a unit highlights its source region, and selecting a region reveals its unit.
priorities.notes: This bidirectional link is the differentiating interaction. It is what makes 'what did the machine actually understand' answerable at a glance.

priorities.statement: Every unit shows which tier produced it and how confident that tier was.
priorities.notes: Confidence is shown honestly, including when the machine is unsure. Hiding it would make the corrections surface pointless.

priorities.statement: A correction creates a new derivation version; it never overwrites the previous reading.
priorities.notes: The audit trail depends on this. The UI must make the versioning visible so a user understands nothing was destroyed.

priorities.statement: Proposed redactions are never applied without explicit confirmation.
An anchor that cannot be resolved says so, rather than highlighting a plausible wrong region.

elements.name: Source page

elements.name: Derived units

elements.name: Anchor highlight
elements.description: The region in the source pane corresponding to the selected unit.

claims.statement: The reader page exposes a named region containing both panes.
Selecting a unit highlights exactly the source region its anchor names.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-021. This is the interaction the whole surface exists for; an approximate highlight is a correctness bug, not a polish issue.

claims.statement: Selecting a source region scrolls its unit into view in the units pane.
claims.rationale: The link has to work in both directions or a reader cannot ask 'what did you make of this paragraph'.

claims.statement: Every unit displays the tier that produced it and its confidence.
An anchor with no alignment to the displayed version renders an explicit notice and highlights nothing.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-019. Silently highlighting a plausible wrong region would make every citation untrustworthy without anyone noticing.

claims.statement: Correcting a unit produces a new derivation version and the version selector reflects it.
claims.rationale: Re-derivation never overwrites. If the UI presented a correction as an in-place edit, users would reasonably assume the old reading was destroyed.

claims.statement: No proposed redaction is applied until the operator confirms it in the dialog.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-010. Automated redaction without human review is not defensible, which is the point of the feature.

claims.statement: Units and their source regions can be traversed by keyboard alone, in both directions.
A screen reader moves from a unit to its corresponding source region in a coherent order.
Loading, populated, low-confidence, unresolved-anchor and error states are reachable and distinct.
